result.topic_en: Equations of motion for the angular-momentum-like quantities g, h, k (Euler-type equations) and their linearization about a state with g=0, p=0, with perturbations expressed in terms of δu and δu'.
result.transcription:
$\frac{\partial g}{\partial t} = rh - qk$
$\frac{\partial h}{\partial t} = -rg + pk$
$\frac{\partial k}{\partial t} = qg - ph$
$g=0,\ p=0$
$\lambda\delta h = -[-q-]r\delta g + \delta p\, k$ $\quad\lambda\delta g = r\delta h - q\delta k + h\delta r - [-k-]{+k+}\delta q$
$\lambda\delta k = +q\delta g - \delta p\, h$
$\delta p = \delta u + \delta u'$ $\quad\delta p_1 = \delta u - \delta u'$
$\delta g = (b+c)^2\delta u + (b-c)^2\delta u'$

methods.what: Euler-type equations of motion for the components g, h, k (rotation vector p, q, r)
methods.quote:
$\frac{\partial g}{\partial t} = rh - qk$
$\frac{\partial h}{\partial t} = -rg + pk$
$\frac{\partial k}{\partial t} = qg - ph$

methods.what: Linearization of these equations about the state g=0, p=0 with perturbations proportional to $e^{\lambda t}$
methods.quote:
$\lambda\delta h = -[-q-]r\delta g + \delta p\, k$ $\quad\lambda\delta g = r\delta h - q\delta k + h\delta r - [-k-]{+k+}\delta q$
$\lambda\delta k = +q\delta g - \delta p\, h$

methods.what: Expression of the perturbations δp, δp_1, δg through new variables δu, δu'
methods.quote:
$\delta p = \delta u + \delta u'$ $\quad\delta p_1 = \delta u - \delta u'$
$\delta g = (b+c)^2\delta u + (b-c)^2\delta u'$
